result:
Posts can now be scheduled to go live later. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass (11 tests, including the new ones), and oxlint reports no problems.

**How it works.** A post has a new optional `published_at` column (nullable ISO 8601 text, like `created_at`). Nothing runs when the time arrives. Each request checks what the viewer may see: posts with no date or a date that has passed, plus the viewer's own scheduled posts. That rule lives in one method, `Post.visibleTo()` in `app/Models/Post.ts`, and the posts list, search and a post's page all use it. A scheduled post's page returns 404 for guests and other users. The home page's "latest posts" now shows only public posts too, since it would otherwise have shown scheduled ones to everyone.

**Form field.** `publishAt` is optional on create and edit. Absent, `null` or empty means publish now; on edit, leaving it empty clears the schedule. Valid values are stored as UTC ISO strings. A value like `next tuesday` is rejected the same way an empty title is, and nothing is saved. The New and Edit pages have a "Publish at" date-and-time field that sends the author's local time as UTC. The list and post page show authors a "Scheduled · goes live …" label, and `publishedAt` is included on every post.

**Report.** `bun run console posts:scheduled` prints `<id>\t<title>\t<published_at>`, soonest first, and exits 0. I ran it against the test database with a past, a near and a far post: stdout held exactly the two future rows. I also ran it against a new, empty database, where migrations run at startup, and stdout was empty. That needed one change beyond the task: the app's startup messages (applied migrations, seeding) used to go to stdout. `bin/console.ts` now sends them to stderr while the app starts, so stdout carries only the command's own output.

- **Which database the report reads:** `bun run console` uses the test database only when `NODE_ENV=test` (or `DATABASE_URL`) points it there. Without either it reads the development database, `./data/guren.db`. If the external check doesn't set one, the report won't see the rows it wrote.
- **Titles containing a tab or newline** would break the one-line-per-post format. They aren't escaped.
- **Leftover test data:** each run of the new tests leaves two test users in the test database; the test post itself is deleted afterwards.

Summary of changes: I added a nullable `published_at` column to `posts` (`db/schema.ts` plus a generated migration in `db/migrations/20260925035719_add_published_at_to_posts/`). I added `Post.visibleTo()` and `Post.scheduled()` in `app/Models/Post.ts` and made `publishedAt` fillable. `PostPayloadSchema` in `app/Http/Validators/PostValidator.ts` gained the optional `publishAt` field. `PostController` stores and updates `publishAt` and filters the list, search and post page by visibility, and `HomeController` shows only public posts. `PostResource` now includes `publishedAt`. The report command is in `app/Console/Commands/ListScheduledPostsCommand.ts`, registered in `src/console.ts`, and `bin/console.ts` sends startup logging to stderr. The React pages (`New`, `Edit`, `Index`, `Show`) got the field and the scheduled label, and I regenerated the `.guren/*.gen.ts` types. New tests are in `tests/ScheduledPosts.test.ts`.
